answer.answer:
Once a product range is highly standardised, three concrete things follow directly, plus a further one requires it as a precondition. Standardisation enables a shift to modular architecture, reduces construction complexity, and supports the ability to accommodate late design changes; it is also a prerequisite (not itself an outcome) for scaling up industrialised construction. What it does not do on its own is guarantee prefabrication, lean workflows or automated production, those show up only as things that tend to co-occur with standardisation across cases, not as consequences it causes.

**Directional effects of standardisation (Highly standardised, AT7):**

- Highly standardised enables Modular architecture: decoupled standardised interfaces enable modular architecture and component interchange [1] (DEP53).
- Highly standardised enables reduced construction complexity: the base module standard reduces component variety and coordinates design, manufacture and assembly [2] (DEP67), backed by a standard-grade source (ISO 2848:1984).
- Highly standardised enables accommodating late design changes: standardisation of interfaces supports interchangeability and system flexibility [3] (DEP90), though the source notes this claim is softened in a terminological review, so treat it as a weaker, qualified link rather than a strong causal finding.

**A precondition relationship, not an outcome:**

- Industrialised-construction scale depends on / requires highly standardised, i.e. industrialised-construction scale depends on standardisation [4] (DEP31). This means standardisation is a requirement to reach industrialised scale, not something standardisation produces by itself; treat industrialised scale as gated on having standardisation in place first.

**Reverse direction worth noting:** modularity itself also feeds back into standardisation. Modular architecture enables highly standardised outcomes because modular architecture reduces the variety of component sizes produced [5] (DEP60), so the modular-standardised relationship runs both ways depending on which is established first.

**What is correlation, not causation:** the graph shows Highly standardised co-occurring with a large set of other enablers across cases, including prefabrication/off-site (PR2, weight 17), mass customisation (PR11, weight 16), lean (PR18, weight 17), DFAB process optimisation (PR1, weight 24), automated production workflow (AR9, weight 24), improved quality (VA3, weight 22), and vertical integration (CO10, weight 18), among 128 co-occurring enablers total. These are statistical associations across deployed cases, not evidence that standardisation causes any of them.

**On deployed cases:** none of the census or RP process records in this context (for example census_RXM5-3, census_RXM4-3, census_RXT4-1) are linked through a dependency or enablement edge to the Highly standardised attribute directly in the material provided, so I cannot point to a specific deployed project that demonstrably achieved modularity, reduced complexity or late-change flexibility because of standardisation. The evidence here is at the enabler-relationship level only.

**Deployed evidence.** The processes in the graph closest to this question, each a real deployment with its record id:
- census_RXM5-3, adopted to address quality; performs concrete work, precast; at technology readiness level 6; developed by Firm_117, Firm_076, Firm_206.
- census_RXM29-4, adopted to address integration, regulation; performs material handling; at technology readiness level 5; developed by Firm_168, Firm_033, Firm_060, Firm_115.
- census_RXM4-3, adopted to address regulation; performs 3d printing, assembly, concrete work, shotcrete; at technology readiness level 7; developed by Firm_115.
- census_RXM5-2, adopted to address quality; performs cast in place, concrete work; at technology readiness level 7; developed by Firm_117, Firm_049.
- census_RXT4-1, adopted to address integration, market, regulation; performs assembly, material handling, timber joinery cutting; at technology readiness level 9; developed by Firm_174.
